citation.title: Topology optimization of 2D structures with nonlinearities using deep learning
citation.authors: Diab W. Abueidda, Seid Koric, Nahil A. Sobh

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: CNN models predict optimized 2D designs without running the iterative optimizer for each query, with negligible inference time.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Inference time is described as negligible, but no classical runtime or speed-up factor is provided.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion says the predicted designs agree well with rigorous nonlinear TO results; test-set mean Dice scores are reported for design similarity.

baseline.implementation: SIMULIA TOSCA called from implicit FEA software; sensitivity-based solver with MMA
baseline.solver: TOSCA sensitivity-based solver / MMA; FE linear solver not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: HPC used for generating optimization data; specific hardware not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: single NVIDIA V100 GPU with 32 GB for training; inference platform described as low-end laptop
baseline.problem_size: 2D design domains; 32 x 32 elements for compared cases
baseline.classical_iterations: iterative TOSCA optimization; stopping count not stated
baseline.ml_time: described as negligible inference time; no value
baseline.training_time: 1.25 h linear and 1.5 h nonlinear on GPU; linear CPU-only 12.5 h (Section 5, Fig. 7)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; datasets generated with TO framework using HPC
baseline.quality_metric: mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) between predicted and ground-truth designs
baseline.quality_gap: mean testing DSC 0.958 (linear) and 0.964 (nonlinear), Sections 5 and Figures 10–11

R1.evidence: Abstract claims negligible inference cost versus iterative optimization, but returned designs are evaluated against ground truth with image-level DSC rather than matched compliance/objective or equal-time results (Sections 5, Figures 10–11).

R2.evidence: Section 2 uses commercial TOSCA with MMA as the classical optimizer; no direct strong-baseline comparison is provided.

R3.evidence: Section 5 reports training durations (1.25 h linear, 1.5 h nonlinear), but does not report dataset-generation cost or a break-even number.

R4.evidence: Sections 5 and Figures 10–11 assess predicted outputs with mean DSC and image examples; returned designs are not reported as FE-verified and failure rates are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: test sets for 3 problem types (linear without stress constraint, linear with stress constraint, nonlinear); sample test sizes not stated in inspected reporting

notes: The queue title matches this work under its earlier title; coded the latest arXiv version, corresponding to the 2020 journal article. A guessed arXiv identifier (1910.08735) resolved to an unrelated cell-segmentation paper; it was not used.
